ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6752, as amended), the Commercial Act (Act No. 3837, as amended), the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit guidelines issued under Financial Services Commission authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry of the Korea Supreme Court (Registration Division)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive routes: (i) for Hague Apostille member states, notarize by Korean notary public, then apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Regional Authentication Office for Apostille; (ii) for non-member states, notarize, have the same MOFA office authenticate the notarial signature, then present to the destination embassy/consulate for consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Status/Registration List)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korea National Tax Service (NTS) and the relevant District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Only one path is effective per receiving state: Hague Apostille via MOFA for member states; consular legalization via MOFA authentication followed by destination consulate for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Directors, duly notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Either obtain Hague Apostille by MOFA for Apostille countries or undergo consular legalization at the destination mission after MOFA authentication; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members of the Yuhan Hoesa, filed with the court registry and notarized if used internationally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive sequence: Apostille by MOFA for member states; MOFA authentication plus consular legalization for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Corporate Account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank, with the account-holding institution's seal and responsible manager signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Generate the letter, have it notarized, then apply exclusively for either Hague Apostille (for members) or consular legalization (for non-members), depending on destination law.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to engagement, the Korean firm must conduct enhanced due diligence on all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and signatories. Screening must cover Korean government watchlists, FATF listings, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals, European Union restrictive measures, and the Korea FIU list of suspected persons of illicit financial activity. Politically Exposed Persons, including foreign and domestic government officials, their immediate family members, and close associates, require senior management approval, source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse media and negative news checks must be documented and retained. Any trigger requires a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Haneul Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Korean Supreme Court, used for corporate name search and reservation; business registration is subsequently coordinated through the Biz-init portal of the National Tax Service.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate names in Korea must be in Hangul. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the suffix yuhan hoesa (meaning limited liability company) must appear at the end of the registered name. Foreign-language elements may be transliterated into Hangul phonetically, and a corresponding Roman-letter name must be declared in the Articles of Association for cross-border documentation. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) mandatory legal form suffix, (2) distinctive main trade name, (3) optional business activity descriptor, and (4) prohibited or sensitive tokens requiring prior authorization. The intertextual correspondence between Hangul and Roman-script versions must be a one-for-one transliteration without addition of descriptive words.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea (when used as state entity name)
Foreign Exchange (without foreign exchange business license)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection to the district court registry within 14 days of notice, explaining why the name is not prohibited, misleading, or identical to an existing registered company under Commercial Act Articles 19 through 24. The registrar must decide within 7 business days. In case of a second rejection, the applicant may appeal administratively to the head of the court administration office and, finally, under the Administrative Litigation Act to the Seoul Administrative Court within 30 days of the final decision. The name reservation may be extended by order of the court for up to an additional 30 days if an appeal is pending and good faith is demonstrated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is accepted by the court registry for filing the registered seat, but the National Tax Service and Korean financial institutions generally reject a mere digital mailbox for tax registration and bank account opening for a professional consultancy under ISIC 7020. The NTS requires an actual physical business location where books and records are kept, and a commercial substance check will be applied. A co-working space or executive office serviced with a full-time local administrator and lease contract may be sufficient; a non-operational mailbox is not permissible unless a supplementary actual workplace is disclosed to the tax office and bank.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (i) registered corporate plaque must be posted at the office entrance; (ii) original lease registration in the company name; (iii) power meters, utility bills, or internet bills showing regular use; (iv) at least one dedicated staff member or director present during business hours; (v) bank statements and NTS e-tax receipts reflecting the registered office address; (vi) if the company operates from a virtual address, a physical administrative office must be listed as a second location. Quantified risk: for a cautiously structured low-risk tax consultancy with full substance, the chance of a municipal tax or registry site inspection within the first 12 months is approximated at 15%; if any red flag is encountered, such as no signboard, absence of staff, or use of a postal drop address, the likelihood escalates to 50% within the same period.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 583 (Limited Liability Company, Yuhan Hoesa), read together with the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Commercial Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office (for example, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office), accessed through the Korean Supreme Court IROS Electronic Registration System; tax-related registration afterwards through the National Tax Service via HomeTax.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) as prescribed by the Korean Commercial Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act. A Yuhan Hoesa may be incorporated with no statutory minimum paid-up capital, provided there is at least one member and one director. All capital stated in the articles of incorporation, if any, must be deposited into a temporary corporate bank account in the company's name before registration is completed. No blocked escrow account requirement exists. Foreign investors must route contributions through a foreign exchange bank and, where applicable, file a Foreign Investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY). Dated: ______, 20__. WHEREAS Yuhan Hoesa will be incorporated as a limited liability company under Articles 543 through 583 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS the founding members have adopted articles of incorporation and have nominated individuals to serve as the initial directors; and WHEREAS the directors must take every lawful action necessary to complete statutory incorporation and to operate an international tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory business falling within ISIC 7020. NOW, THEREFORE, the undersigned directors and founding members hereby resolve as follows. 1. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [address], Republic of Korea, and the Company shall display its corporate name, adopt its corporate seal, and record such office in all contracts, invoices, tax filings, and banking records. 2. Capital Subscription. The paid-in capital appearing in the articles of incorporation, namely [amount in Korean won], is ratified and approved. The directors are directed to deposit the full amount of stated capital into a temporary incorporation account at a licensed Korean commercial bank, obtain the bank's capital contribution receipt, and hold the funds exclusively for the Company pending issuance of the certificate of incorporation. 3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. Effective immediately upon incorporation registration, the following persons are appointed: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name] as Director; and, if required or considered prudent, [Name] as Statutory Auditor. Each officer shall exercise the powers granted by the Commercial Act and the Company's articles. 4. Banking Mandate. The Company's principal bankers shall be [bank name, if selected]. The Representative Director, acting jointly with one other authorized director, is authorized to open corporate current accounts, to execute signature cards, to direct wire and card payment rail arrangements, and to sign all banking and treasury documentation. Transfers exceeding [threshold] shall require dual signatures. 5. Tax and Professional Registration. The CEO is directed to register the Company with the National Tax Service through HomeTax, obtain the Business Registration Certificate and corporate tax identification number, and procure that any statutory tax agency service is delivered through or with a licensed Certified Tax Accountant where the law so requires. 6. Seals and Certification. The CEO is authorized to file the incorporation registration application, to execute and file all registration declarations, to produce certified excerpts, and to take all incidental actions necessary to bring the Company into legal existence. This resolution takes effect immediately and may be produced as a veritable corporate act in any governmental, judicial, banking, or notarial context. The directors shall retain a signed minute evidencing this unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Execution of Notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Information Center of the Supreme Court of Korea (IROS) via www.iros.go.kr; Notary Public at the Korean Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding member or the authorized foreign-investment attorney must select the corporate name in Korean and, if desired, a romanized English equivalent, and verify on IROS that the name is not confusingly identical to an existing registered Korean legal person. After clearance, articles of incorporation must be prepared under Articles 543 through 583 of the Commercial Act, stating the corporate purpose, registered office location, stated capital, contribution amounts and values, member identities, duration, officer structure, and meeting requirements. Every founding member must execute the articles of incorporation. The executed instrument should then be notarized by a Korean notary public to obtain the certificate of authentication needed for court registration, bank account opening, and subsequent issue of the certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Passport or foreign national identification card of each founding member
Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean, with certified Korean translation if the original is foreign
Power of attorney, notarized and apostilled, if the application is submitted by an agent
IROS name availability search report or printout
Statement of corporate purpose and preliminary business plan for the Korean regulator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or deceptively similar, the applicant must submit two alternative names through the same IROS process. If the notary raises translation or content deficiencies, the articles must be amended by a new execution page and returned for notarization without restarting the main application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Deposit and Bank Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Banking Department of a licensed Korean commercial bank (for example, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, or Hana Bank); Foreign Exchange Bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for inbound remittances
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must open a temporary incorporation deposit account in the name of the proposed Yuhan Hoesa at a Korean financial institution. Each subscriber must remit the contribution amount stated in the articles of incorporation. Foreign-investor funds must be remitted through a foreign exchange bank and supported by a foreign exchange declaration or, where applicable, an investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The bank will issue a capital contribution certificate confirming that the full stated capital has been deposited for the account of the company. This certificate is an indispensable annex to the court registration application. After the certificate of incorporation has been issued, the temporary account is converted into the permanent corporate operating account, subject to completion of the bank's customer due diligence procedures.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or government-issued identity documents of the subscribers
Foreign exchange declaration or foreign investment report
Bank account application forms and corporate fact sheet
Proof of proposed registered office address, such as a lease agreement
Wire transfer confirmation or credit receipt for each contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises an anti-money laundering query, the subscribers must supply a detailed source-of-funds declaration, an organizational chart showing ultimate beneficial ownership, and a sworn statement explaining the purpose of the funds. If the foreign exchange declaration is rejected, the remitting member must refile with amended remittance purpose codes and, if necessary, select a different licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the Local District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office (Registration Section) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court IROS Electronic Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the bank certificate of paid-in capital is received, the representative director or authorized agent must file the Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa with the registry office of the competent district court. The filing must be submitted using the statutory form and accompanied by the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, written consents of the appointed directors and auditor to act, and evidence of the registered office such as a lease certificate or real-estate register excerpt. The registrar examines the application for formal and substantive legal compliance. Registration tax, education surtax, and court filing fees must be paid through the court's revenue assessment or the electronic payment module. If the registry determines that all legal prerequisites are satisfied, it issues the certificate of registered company, thereby completing the formation of the Yuhan Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital contribution issued by the deposit bank
Written consent of each director and auditor to assume office
Proof of registered office, including lease agreement or certified real estate register excerpt
Certified copy of the power of attorney and identity documents
Receipt of payment of registration tax and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a corrective order or suspension notice, the applicant must cure the cited defect within the prescribed period, generally three to seven days, by filing a supplementary document or amendment. If the defect involves a substantive provision of the articles, the members must adopt a correcting meeting resolution and re-file immediately. If the filing is rejected, appeal is available by a new application supported by a certified explanatory memorandum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea; District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after the court registration is completed, the representative director must file for business registration with the National Tax Service using the HomeTax online portal. The application must include the company's registered corporate identification number, articles of incorporation, registered office address, and statutory officer information. The National Tax Service verifies the company's identity and address, then issues the Business Registration Certificate, which includes the corporation's tax identification number. This certificate is needed for value-added tax invoicing, corporate income tax returns, bank account activation, customs declarations if any, and client due diligence in the tax advisory sector. A foreign-owned company without domestic effective management should concurrently appoint and register a statutory tax representative.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form via HomeTax
Certificate of incorporation issued by the district court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or other proof of registered office
Passport or alien registration card of the representative director
Tax representative appointment letter, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If HomeTax rejects the application on the ground of insufficient address or identity documents, the representative must appear at the district tax office with the original lease, certificate of incorporation, and passport, and request manual verification. If the tax ID is suspended for non-filing, the company must file all missed returns and apply for restoration of the business registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Final Corporate Settlement Account and AML/KYC Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Banking and Compliance Department of the selected Korean commercial bank; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) regulatory framework under the Financial Transactions Reports Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Business Registration Certificate is obtained, the temporary incorporation account must be converted into a standing corporate settlement account. The representative director and any additional authorized director must appear before the bank's corporate desk, submit the company registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, officer identity documents, and an ultimate beneficial ownership declaration. The bank will conduct enhanced due diligence consistent with the Financial Action Task Force recommendations, particularly because the company provides tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory services, which may serve higher-risk business clients. The final banking mandate must designate dual signatories, payment thresholds, and permitted payment rails. For the company's target rails, bank wire and credit-card acceptance must be documented through a merchant acquiring agreement and the approved corporate account. Once the account is active, the company may begin issuing invoices and receiving international bank wires.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate of the National Tax Service
Certificate of incorporation from the district court
Corporate seal certificate
Board resolution designating signatories and banking mandate
Passport or alien registration cards of all authorized signatories
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and corporate organizational chart
Payment gateway or merchant acquiring agreement setting out bank wire and credit card acceptance terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or KoFIU requests enhanced due diligence because of the tax advisory nature of the entity, the company must supply a client intake policy, anti-money laundering procedures, expected client profile, and regulatory authorization references. The matter may be escalated to the bank's central compliance officer; if the bank still declines, the company may quickly open an account at another licensed institution and provide a remediated compliance file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (District Tax Office) for the mandatory Business Registration Certificate; Seoul Metropolitan Government Business Licensing Information for any office signage and local permits; Korean Tax Accountants Association for supervision of licensed certified tax accountants engaged in tax agency activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate issued under the Framework Act on National Taxes; no separate industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required because ISIC 7020 is a pure consulting and tax advisory activity. Where the company performs statutory tax agency services, it must engage a Certified Tax Accountant registered with the Korean Tax Accountants Association under the Certified Tax Accountant Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Korea Environment Corporation — Not Applicable to this service-only entity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. ISIC 7020 is an office-based management consulting and tax structuring activity with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, warehousing, or land reclamation. The Environmental Impact Assessment Act does not trigger any Full EIA report, preliminary EIA, or environmental registration requirement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The entity has no industrial wastewater discharge point, VOC emission stack, or hazardous waste generation source. No permits are required under the Clean Air Conservation Act or the Water Quality Preservation Act. Ordinary office waste must be collected by a licensed municipal waste contractor under the Waste Management Act, and any electronic waste must be recycled through an approved recycler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: As a pure office activity, only standard fire prevention and workplace health measures apply. The leased office must obtain a fire-fighting systems inspection certificate and evacuation plan approval from the local fire station under the National Fire Agency of Korea and the Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Fire-Fighting Systems. No structural-load inspection or industrial workplace permit is required unless the company installs high-density storage racks or heavy security vaults. The employer must register with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service for workers' compensation and employment insurance and must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office workstations, ventilation, and electrical safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax System electronic portal (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business in South Korea must appoint a tax representative (a resident individual or local corporation) registered with the NTS. The representative must apply to the district tax office having jurisdiction over the representative's business location or the Seoul National Tax Service for non-residents for a Business Registration Certificate using the standard application for business registration. The application must confirm the foreign entity's constitutional documents, foreign tax identification number, and proof of a Korean bank account used for tax payments. Upon approval, the NTS issues a Business Registration Number (SINBRI) which serves as the corporate tax ID and value-added tax ID. The foreign entity is then required to comply with all periodic filing, e-invoice, and payment obligations through the tax representative or through a fixed place of business if one is established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not maintain a check-the-box or hybrid entity classification election analogous to the US Treasury regulations. A Yuhan Hoesa is always treated as a taxable domestic corporation, subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act and to the Value-Added Tax Act as a supply business.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0. Any person independently supplying taxable goods or services in South Korea must register for VAT before commencing business, irrespective of expected turnover. However, a non-resident engaged only in exports or qualifying cross-border services with no domestic taxable supply may not be required to obtain a Korean VAT registration unless the supply is subject to Korean VAT under the reverse charge or has a fixed establishment in Korea. The annual turnover threshold for simplified taxation for small individual entrepreneurs is KRW 80,000,000, but this does not exempt registration for corporations or foreign entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses are required to issue and transmit electronic tax invoices through the HomeTax System for all business-to-business supplies of taxable goods or services. The NTS operates a real-time anti-fraud clearance mechanism in which every e-tax invoice must be transmitted to HomeTax within one day of the supply date. Cash receipts are mandatory for retail supplies exceeding KRW 100,000, with mandatory real-time reporting. Tax invoices for exports must be issued and the export details reported in the electronic taxation of exports. There is no fiscal stamping or government pre-clearance of individual VAT invoices; instead the NTS uses continuous validation, data matching against customs declarations, and automatic cross-checks to detect suppressed or false invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% is applied to the export of goods when the goods are taken out of South Korea under an export declaration, and to services supplied to a place outside South Korea where the benefit of the services is consumed outside Korea. Qualifying services include international transport, services physically rendered outside Korea, and digital or consulting services provided to foreign non-resident clients with no taxable domestic use. The exporter must keep full documentary evidence of the exporter's identity, the customer's identity, the export contract, delivery terms, and proof that the goods actually left Korea. For offshore digital services supplied by a foreign business to a Korean customer, the domestic customer may be subject to reverse-charge VAT; exports by Korean suppliers must meet the place-of-supply rules and supporting foreign exchange documentation to claim 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Certificate) prepared and lodged through UNI-PASS and confirmed by Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual shipment out of Korea

Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Confirmation (including Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate or FIRC-equivalent issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank) evidencing collection of foreign currency export proceeds
Export sales invoice matched to the customs declaration and the underlying purchase order or contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service will deny zero-rating and retroactively assess VAT at 10% plus statutory interest if the export is later determined to be fictitious, unsubstantiated, or not economically real. The attraction or wrongful receipt of VAT refunds on unverified zero-rated exports triggers penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on Taxes: up to 40% of the unpaid or evaded tax for fraudulent claims, or up to 20% for negligent unfaithful filing. Additional penalties apply for failure to issue electronic tax invoices, failure to transmit them within the statutory deadline, and foreign exchange law violations for unrepatriated export proceeds. The NTS may refer egregious cases to the public prosecutor's office for criminal tax evasion proceedings, resulting in imprisonment and additional fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service (KCS) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized yet strictly monitored foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won (KRW) is generally convertible for current account transactions, including consultancy fees, dividends, and trade-related payments, but capital account operations such as equity investment in a local entity, acquisition of domestic debt instruments, or cross-border loans are subject to filing or reporting requirements with the designated foreign exchange bank, and in certain cases, prior approval from the MOEF/BOK. A statutory surrender requirement exists for export of goods and services: all export proceeds must be received in foreign currency and either sold to a domestic bank within the prescribed period or deposited into a foreign currency account; service exporters, including management consultancy firms, must adhere to a six-month collection and settlement deadline unless an extension is granted. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permissible upon presentation of audited financial statements and tax clearance, but anti-money-laundering (AML) screening and beneficial ownership declarations add a two-to-four-week bank compliance cycle. In practice, repatriation of capital gains and dividends requires a foreign exchange certificate of transaction (performance confirmation) issued by the receiving bank, and any hedging instrument must be tied to an underlying real demand to avoid speculative classification. The overall regime is best described as current-account open, capital-account managed, with high transparency and strong penalties for non-reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds (including consultant service invoices billed to overseas clients) must be collected within six months (or one year for projects approved by the MOEF) from the date of export. There is no mandatory forced conversion to KRW; if the exporter maintains a domestic foreign-currency account, the receipts can be retained, but the bank must be notified and the transaction reported to the Korea Customs Service via the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Any extension beyond the statutory period requires an ex-ante or ex-post approval depending on the reason, such as delayed payment due to inspection or litigation. For KRW settlement needs, the exporter may sell the foreign currency to a domestic bank at the prevailing market rate with no prior approval required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (foreign investment) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW)
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not viable as primary banking providers for a Korean registered entity. The Korean financial regulatory framework does not confer passporting rights to foreign EMIs and any entity performing money transfer services, payment gateway operations, or FX intermediation in KRW without a license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act (EFTA) and the Real Name Financial Transaction Act is committing an unlicensed foreign-exchange activity. A statutory Korean corporation must maintain its transactional banking relationship with a licensed domestic bank for capital escrow, operational KRW settlement, and trade-related fees. Offshore EMIs can only be used incidentally for employee perks or outbound small-value credit card top-ups, but they cannot act as the treasury rails for corporate disbursements or inbound capital. The compliance risk of routing client consultancy fees through an unlicensed EMI triggers debanking by Korean counterparties and potential criminal liability under FETA Article 8; therefore the treasury blueprint forbids such routing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Yuhan Hoesa with a non-resident director or shareholder, the designated foreign exchange bank will require in-branch physical appearance of the statutory director and the beneficial owner for the opening of a capital escrow (foreign investment) account. A face-to-face interview with the compliance officer is mandatory when the foreign investor is a corporate entity from a high-risk jurisdiction or when the controller is not personally identifiable from public registries. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for the initial capital escrow account; however, once the entity has operated for one full financial year and the bank relationship is seasoned, an additional operational KRW account may be opened through a notarized power of attorney with apostille and a remote video call, provided the bank's risk-based policy permits it. For the statutory Yuhan Hoesa registration, the domestic resident manager must provide a physical presence in Korea; that individual can also serve as the bank signatory if appointed as the 'in-country responsible person' for FX reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a lawyer or politically exposed person (PEP) participating in tax structuring, and the beneficial chain includes trust-like elements from a non-Egmont jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified source-of-wealth statement from the UBO's asset management institution, a full breakdown of the equity chain in the Yuhan Hoesa registration form, a corporate chart with all intermediate entities, certified passport copies with apostille, and a written explanation signed by the in-country resident manager confirming the commercial purpose of the tax consulting business and the absence of shell-only income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border fee flows are expected from the US parent to the Korean subsidiary with a transfer pricing arrangement above the intercompany safe harbor, triggering bank suspicion of round-tripping or aggressive tax avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the transfer pricing policy documentation (Master File, Local File, and benchmarking study prepared under OECD guidelines), the signed intercompany service agreement with a fee schedule and time sheets, the prior-year corporate tax returns of the parent and subsidiary, and a certificate of tax residence for any treaty relief claim.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The initial capital contribution to the Yuhan Hoesa is routed in multiple tranches from a third-country bank not on the FATF white list, leading to anomalous transaction-pattern flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce the escrow instruction letter signed by the Korean bank, the foreign investment registration certificate (foreign-investment report) filed with KOTRA or the exchange bank, a bank-to-bank confirmation letter with the remitting bank's SWIFT BIC and transaction reference, invoices or subscription agreement proving the legal origin of funds, and a detailed board resolution approving the funding plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Korean bank compliance rejects the director's appointment if the foreign director lacks a clear 'residential address' in a country with incomplete beneficial ownership registries, creating an identity verification gap.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence must include a recently notarized certificate of personal identity from a recognized government authority (apostilled), a utility bill or bank statement in the director's name showing the current address, a medical or criminal background verification from the home jurisdiction, and an executed director's indemnity and resignation waiver filed with the Korean court registration office.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Yuhan Hoesa must be wired from the remitting shareholder via SWIFT MT103 with a purpose code compliant with the Korean Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS), typically '821101 - Acquisition of equity shares' for paid-in capital or '821201 - Long-term loan' for shareholder subordinated debt. The remittance must be received at a licensed foreign exchange bank before the filing of the foreign-investment report is completed; the bank will issue a 'certificate of foreign direct investment' after funds are credited and the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) acknowledgment is obtained. For capital verification under the Commercial Act, a certified public accountant (CPA) statement must reference the bank receipt and the foreign exchange register number. The exchange bank will independently check that the remitter matches the UBO name on the shareholder register, the purpose code matches the statutory scope, and no mixing occurs with third-party strings. All incoming wires must avoid using personal remittance codes or omitting the corporate registration number, as that leads to suspension and possible conversion penalty.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury operations will use three primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for operational fees, licensing royalties, and management consultancy invoices where the beneficiary invoice contains a clear economic rationale; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) when the Korean entity purchases software licenses or digital content with a physical deliverable, enabling the bank to verify shipment and invoice; and (3) Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) for smaller trade contracts with trusted counterparties, reducing bank charges but preserving traceability. For every outbound payment above USD 5,000, the Korean bank requires a supporting invoice, contract, and the appropriate FEIS purpose code (e.g., '321201 - Management fees' for cross-border management consulting, or '321302 - R&D services' if applicable). Cross-border disbursements in KRW are not permitted as a default; settlements must be effectuated in USD, EUR, or a fully convertible currency, and the Korean bank will convert the underlying KRW deposit at the rate published by the Seoul Money Brokerage Services on the value date. Any payment to a tax haven jurisdiction or a blacklisted bank is automatically held for manual AML review, so the treasury team must maintain a counterparty whitelist in the KYC system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward FX contracts with maturities up to 12 months for hedging real trade receivables or payables, requiring a confirmed invoice and a bank-approved underlying exposure form under FETA guidelines.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for off-shore entities hedging KRW exposure; the Korean Yuhan Hoesa itself cannot access the onshore NDF market, but its parent may use NDFs offshore to synthetically hedge the subsidiary's net profit repatriation, provided the contract is executed with a global bank that has no onshore KRW position.

Currency swaps with a maturity exceeding 12 months and associated with long-term intercompany loans from the parent to the Yuhan Hoesa, subject to MOEF filing when the swap notional exceeds the debt-to-equity safe harbor threshold (currently 150% under the Korean tax code).

Zero-cost collars and vanilla options on USD/KRW with a maximum tenor of 12 months, solely for hedging the forecasted annual consulting fee receipts from US and European clients, requiring board-approved hedging policy and monthly valuation reporting to the bank's Treasury Division.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and attached financial statements, including the actual controller disclosure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal year-end, within three months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underreporting or failing to file triggers negligence penalties of 10%-40% of the understated tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus a daily late-payment interest charge of 0.022% on every unpaid day; chronic non-filing enables forced collection, seizure of corporate assets, business closure, and administrative strike-off/dissolution of the corporate registration for a dormant company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return on the local residence surtax (local income tax on corporate earnings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Si/Gun/Gu local government via WETAX local e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year corporations, by April 30; for non-calendar fiscal years, within four months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers local additional taxes of up to 20% plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; continued delinquency allows asset attachment and administrative cancellation of the company's business tax registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of members to approve the annual financial statements and to decide on appropriation of profits or losses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate governance record kept at the registered office; minutes entered in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e., by June 30 for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors in default may be fined up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act, may be disqualified for continued management, and may become civilly liable for loss arising from failure to call the meeting; profits cannot be lawfully distributed until approved financial statements exist

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public auditor's report on the annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) for e-filing, with a copy attached to the National Tax Service corporate income tax return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before the ordinary meeting of members; the audit report must be submitted to FSS within two weeks after the meeting and no later than the statutory six-month annual-report window for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain the required audit is punishable by imprisonment up to three years or a criminal fine up to KRW 50 million under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others; FSS may appoint a designated auditor and impose corrective orders, and NTS may disregard unaudited financial statements in tax assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise annual maintenance and status report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year; for December year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report may expose the foreign investor to an administrative fine up to KRW 10 million, the loss of foreign-investment protection benefits, repatriation privileges and statutory tax/financial incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll tax settlement and social insurance wage-base declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (for income withholding) and the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Employment Insurance Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Year-end tax settlement remittance by March 10 for withholding taxes; annual wage-base and contribution declarations to social-insurance carriers by March 15; monthly withholding returns and contributions due by the 10th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withheld income tax not remitted triggers 10%-20% additional taxes, 0.022% daily interest, and criminal sanctions; unpaid social insurance contributions generate late charges, restrictions on government financing programs, and administrative seizure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate registration maintenance and registered-office/change filings (event-driven, not an annual renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Court Registry (Registration Office) under the Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Changes in director, member, registered address, existence, or corporate name must be filed within two weeks of the triggering event; no periodic renewal filing exists in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register changes is punishable by an administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million and the company cannot assert the unregistered change against a bona fide third party; extended non-use or non-payment of public dues can lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a private Yuhan Hoesa, a mandatory independent CPA audit is required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others (with conforming application to limited liability companies) when the company's total assets as of the fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.1 million). Companies holding financial, securities, investment advisory, or other expressly regulated licenses, and publicly listed entities, are subject to mandatory audit regardless of asset size. The Presidential Enforcement Decree further applies a designated-company quantitative test covering revenue and headcount, requiring the annual audit where both the Decree's revenue threshold and the 100-or-more average-employee condition are met; this combined threshold must be retested each fiscal year-end.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) is mandatory for all externally audited public companies; a privately-held Yuhan Hoesa below the audit threshold may apply Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards, but once the statutory audit trigger is crossed, K-IFRS or the specific GAAP applicable to the licensing authority must be used consistently for the statutory audit opinion.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not maintain a stand-alone annual UBO registry return for a private Yuhan Hoesa. However, the Commercial Act obliges the company to keep an up-to-date Register of Members at the registered office, and all membership transfers, pledges, or changes in actual control become legally effective only when reflected in that register. For income-tax and foreign-exchange purposes, transfers of domestic equities and changes in beneficial ownership must be reported to the National Tax Service and, where the payee or acquirer is non-resident, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act within 30 days of the transaction; the annual corporate income tax return must also include the actual controller disclosure. The company is therefore expected to conduct an annual UBO confirmation exercise before the CIT due date, verifying the natural-person beneficiaries, shareholding percentages, and no disqualifying statuses.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per annum, depending on the registered office provider and local secretarial firm
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if the KRW 12 billion asset threshold is not met; USD 15,000 - USD 45,000 for a small or mid-sized Yuhan Hoesa once a statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% progressive corporate income tax rate (10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on the next KRW 200 million; 22% on the next KRW 280 billion; 25% above KRW 300 billion) plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax, resulting in a combined marginal headline rate of 27.5% for large taxable income brackets
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under the Korean Special Cases Taxation Control Act (SCTCA), qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones may obtain 100% or 50% corporate tax reductions for 3-5 years and 2 years of 50% reductions thereafter, subject to investment thresholds and minimum employment conditions; additionally, qualifying R&E expenditures are eligible for a 25% tax credit on the excess over the average of prior years, and certain venture/start-up companies enjoy 50% tax rate reductions for the first 5 years; Korea does not operate a standalone patent box regime, but income from qualified patented technology may be captured through the R&D expense credit and the foreign-related intangible income adjustment rules

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form 110-1 (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) filed electronically through HomeTax System (HTS) operated by the National Tax Service (NTS), including attached schedules for tax adjustments, reconciliation statements, and transfer pricing disclosures
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end plus 3 months for the annual tax return (e.g., a December 31 fiscal year-end is due on March 31 of the following year); corporations with an advance tax year-end must file within 3 months of the appointed closing date; quarterly advance corporate tax payments are due within 2 months after the end of each six-month advance payment period on June 30 and December 31, meaning an interim return must be filed by August 31 and February 28 respectively

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification and statutory profile: corporate registration number (business registration number), legal form (Yuhan Hoesa/LLC), head office address, representative director name, tax period (beginning and end dates), ISIC 7020 business code, and consolidated or non-consolidated filing marker
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean resident fully-owned or branch entity owned by non-residents, enter the Korean corporate registration number and check the non-consolidated standard filing box; a foreign-owned Korean resident Yuhan Hoesa must disclose the ultimate foreign parent's jurisdiction and permanent establishment status in the attachment schedule for foreign shareholding and foreign management information; ensure the closed Korean business code 7020 is entered as the primary business activity, as th is affects the applicable industry-specific tax audit selection algorithm

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book income before tax adjustments derived from the statutory balance sheet and income statement prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or Korean GAAP, representing pre-tax profit or loss of the resident corporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For cross-border tax structuring advisory company, record all domestic and foreign-source revenue net of attributable expenses; non-resident owners must ensure that intercompany management fees and headquarters charges are recognized in accordance with the arms length principle before arriving at net book income; any deferred revenue from multi-year consultancy engagements must be recognized using the percentage-of-completion method for services; avoid understatement of cross-border digital content or gaming royalties in this box because the NTS performs automated matching with e-tax invoice data

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment - non-deductible expenses added back to net income, including disallowed entertainment expenses, fines and penalties, bribes, donations in excess of statutory limits, depreciation in excess of prescribed rates, excessive or non-substantiated headcount allocations, and corporate taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-related intra-group service fees are deductible only if supported by contemporaneous service agreements (usually in English/Korean), actual performance documentation, invoice records, and a showing that the fee is not a constructive distribution of profits; management fees paid to foreign headquarters must pass the 'duplicated service' test to be deductible; conservative treatment: add back all service fees that lack concrete evidence, and separately annex the service charge worksheets and fee structure approvals

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment - non-taxable income and tax-exempt items deducted from net income, including dividend income under the participation exemption regime, foreign-source income already taxed at subsidiary level, certain capital gains from founder stock transactions, and other treaty-recognized tax-exempt profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from overseas subsidiaries are not automatically exempt; the participation exemption requires at least 25% ownership for at least 18 months and that the subsidiary is not a passive investment vehicle in a tax haven; for non-resident-owned Korean entity, dividend inflow from a foreign affiliate should be supported by tax authority certificates and audited financial statements; do not claim treaty reduced withholding tax on the domestic Korean source dividends in Box 4 unless the entity is conducting direct investment; attach Schedule 4 of the tax return with the dividends-sourced computation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income before loss carryforward (interim tax base) calculated as: Box 2 + Box 3 - Box 4; also includes adjustments required for transfer pricing contraventions, hidden undistributed profits, and thin-capitalization interest disallowance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent's unrelated shareholder loans will trigger Korea's thin-capitalization rule: excess interest paid on loans from a foreign controlling shareholder is non-deductible if the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 150% (or 200% for financial institutions); therefore, before computing Box 5, add back excess interest on intercompany debt from the foreign parent or affiliated lenders; transfer pricing adjustments resulting from NTS audits or voluntary adjustments must be reflected in this box; obtain a tax adjustment working paper from a certified tax accountant (CTA) to support the computation of this line

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deduction: current-year application of the 15-year loss carryforward from prior year tax returns, limited to 60% of the current-year taxable income for large corporations (80% for small and medium enterprises)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from the same legal entity (KR_YUHANGHOESA) may be carried forward; a newly established foreign-owned LLC cannot inherit losses of a predecessor; for foreign investors acquiring a Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the loss carryforward remains with the legal entity but loses value if there is an ownership change above 50% within a short period due to anti-loss trafficking rules; attach schedule of tax losses per year and the computation of the reclaimed loss amount; note that NTS will independently verify loss years against prior filings and may deny the deduction if the transfer occurred for tax avoidance purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (tax base) after loss deduction, i.e., Box 5 minus Box 6, which is the final tax base subject to the progressive corporate tax rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the taxable income is positive-rounded in KRW; for a Korean resident Yuhan Hoesa owned by non-residents, the tax base is based on worldwide income, not just Korean-source income; allocate income based on the permanent establishment rules if the Korean entity operates as a branch of a foreign company; no special non-resident preferential taxable base exists for a Korean resident corporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax calculated on the taxable income in Box 7 using progressive rates applied to each bracket, before foreign tax credits and other credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the rates correctly: 10% up to KRW 200M, 20% on the next KRW 200M, 22% on the next KRW 280B, and 25% above KRW 300B; then calculate the 10% local income tax as a surcharge on the national corporate tax, which is reported on a separate line of the same return with the local tax schedule; for non-resident-owned entities, this tax is payable in Korean won; timing: base the calculation on monthly provisional payments already made (July provisional payments and year-end adjustments) to avoid underpayment interest

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reductions: foreign tax credits for eligible foreign taxes paid by the Korean resident corporation, R&D tax credits for qualifying research expenses, employment tax credits, temporary investment tax credits, and credits arising under tax treaty settlement agreements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are capped at the Korean corporate tax attributable to the foreign-source income; attach the certified tax computation table (Form 110-4 and related schedules) showing the foreign tax base and the amount of foreign tax paid to overseas authorities; non-resident investors should remember that the foreign tax credit belongs to the Korean corporation, not to the foreign shareholders; any excess credit may be carried forward for 5 years, but cannot be converted into a refund; digital content companies with foreign withholding on export revenues should evidence foreign tax certificates and treaty reductions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional corporate income tax for under-distributed retained earnings applicable to domestic companies owned by foreign-staffed shells (criminal risk), and alternative minimum tax (AMT) equal to 10% of the difference between higher governmental tax and regular tax for certain corporations, applied when credits push the effective tax rate below the statutory floor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box is critically relevant for cross-border structuring entities: if the Korean entity is characterized as a 'shell' with no real economic activity, no employees, and no business premises, the NTS may invoke the corporate substance-over-form doctrine to deny treaty benefits and impose the anti-avoidance corporate tax at 30% of the distributed dividends for non-residents; additionally, the alternative minimum tax (AMT) should be tested when utilizing accumulated credits; ensure that the company's actual employment and office lease records are attached to avoid the automatic applicability of AMT and shell-company surcharges

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax due (national corporate income tax plus local income tax surcharge) after application of advance interim payments, withholding credits, and any prepayments; this is the final liability payable to the NTS
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean resident Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, ensure the proper discounting of the interim paid tax amounts (June 30 and December 31 payments) and any withholding tax on Korean-source income paid to the corporation; make payment in Korean won to the designated NTS bank account; if a refund is claimed, attach the bank account certification form (preferably a Korean bank account in the entity's registered name); a mismatch between the advanced payments and final tax results in a daily interest charge of 0.022% on the underpayment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DTA relief and non-resident withholding reconciliation: record the total amount of tax withheld at source by Korean withholding agents on income paid by the Korean entity to non-residents, including bank interest credited to a foreign account, remitted dividends, and royalties, and reconcile the withholding tax remitted to NTS during the year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: While this box appears as an information line on the Korean corporate income tax return, it triggers the non-resident income tax reconciliation schedule; cross-border payments to non-residents on the following streams attract withholding at source: dividends paid to shareholders (22%, or reduced treaty rate where applicable), interest paid to foreign lenders (22%, or treaty rate), and royalties for intellectual property and proprietary software (22%, or treaty rate); the Korean entity acts as withholding agent, remits the withholding tax, and quarterly withholds under Article 156 of the Corporate Income Tax Act; any failure to withhold for a non-resident triggers a strict personal civil/criminal enforcement against the director as the obligated on-site administrator

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a corporate income tax return by the statutory deadline triggers: (i) a blanket non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax, (ii) an understatement penalty ranging from 10% to 30% of the understated tax depending on egregiousness (gross understatement 30%); (iii) daily overdue surcharge of 0.022% per day on the unpaid tax using a 365-day annual rate; (iv) a false tax invoice penalty of 2% of the invoice amount; and (v) criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act if the tax evaded exceeds KRW 300 million (imprisonment up to 7 years or fine up to 3 times the evaded tax). Corporate directors and compliance officers are personally liable for the unpaid taxes plus penalties where they intentionally concealed cross-border income or failed to submit required transfer pricing documents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on the dividend payment to a non-resident shareholder, composed of 20% corporate income tax withheld under Article 98 of the Corporate Income Tax Act plus 2% local income tax surcharge; this rate applies before any Double Tax Agreement (DTA) reduction, with withholding and remittance due on the 10th day of the month following the dividend distribution
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty-reduced withholding on Korean-source dividends, the Korean-resident paying corporation must file a request with the National Tax Service through the HomeTax system using the 'Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction and Withholding Tax Exemption Approval' (Form 1215 series) accompanied by: (1) an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority of the beneficial owner for the fiscal year in which the dividend is paid; (2) a beneficial ownership statement from the ultimate non-resident parent proving the recipient is not an agent, nominee, or conduit; (3) a shareholding and holding-period statement showing the ownership threshold and the 18-month minimum holding period (e.g., 25% ownership or lower treaty threshold) is satisfied; (4) a brief economic substance declaration with details of local staff, business premise and decision-making in the residence country; if the application is not submitted before each payment, the 22% domestic withholding must be remitted and the refund route is the ordinary NTS refund procedure with a 2-month processing period; Korean law applies the 'look-through' approach and a treaty-shopping restriction on companies with no substance in the treaty state; recently, the NTS demands a certificate from the foreign tax authority confirming the TRC was issued after scrutiny of the recipient's filings and actual place of effective management.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty payments for industrial, commercial, scientific equipment, and copyrighted software/know-how attract statutory 22% withholdings (20% national + 2% local). Under the Korea-OECD Model-based DTAs, most treaties apply a 10% withholding rate on royalties and interest, but the reduced rate depends on beneficial ownership, with some treaties allowing 0% or reduced interest for financial institutions; non-resident must provide a TRC and a beneficial owner declaration to the withholding agent before payment; interest paid to a non-resident on an intercompany loan is eligible for the treaty rate only if the structure is not subject to the thin-capitalization disallowance; royalties for the use of intellectual property in Korea are sourced in Korea even for non-resident licensors, and failure to withhold invites interest, penalties, and criminal liability.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Articles 6(5) and 7 of the International Tax Adjustment Act and Enforcement Decree provisions, a taxpayer engaged in international related-party transactions must prepare a Local File if the annual intercompany transaction value exceeds KRW 5 billion, and a Master File if its consolidated annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and total international related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; in addition, a short-form local report is required for transactions exceeding KRW 1 billion, and a data submission deadline of 60 days upon NTS request (not less than 30 days) applies for the ordinary documentation; failure to submit contemporaneous TP documentation may result in a 20% penalty of the claimed adjustment amount and a discretionary portion from the NTS in determining the arm's length price
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply the specific OECD Economic Substance Requirements for zero-tax jurisdictions; instead, the national doctrine of substance-over-form, reinforced by the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) in Article 6(2) of the International Tax Adjustment Act and the 'effective management and control' test, allows the tax authority to recharacterize transactions or deny a claimed treaty benefit where the Korean resident company or the foreign owner lacks the functional profile (people, premises, core income-generating activities) expected of a true intermediary; for a cross-border advisory firm such as ISIC 7020, the NTS will scrutinize whether the Korean entity is the principal engaged in the CIGA (negotiating contracts, billing clients, bearing economic risks, and employing substantive senior consultants) rather than an instrument of a foreign principal; if substance is deemed insufficient, the income is reattributed to the non-resident principals, the treaty withholding exemptions are denied, and the corporate veil of the Yuhan Hoesa is pierced for WHT and criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion through omission of cross-border income and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A director of KR_YUHANGHOESA intentionally omits fees for services rendered to offshore clients by having the clients remit payment to a foreign bank account of a shadow affiliate, while classifying the Korean entity as a shell; as a result, the Korean corporate income tax return omits the entire revenue stream from the cross-border tax structuring advisory business, and the director signs the annual Form 110-1 knowing the statement is false
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violates Articles 9 and 10 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and Article 14 of the same Act: the sanction is imprisonment for up to 7 years or a fine of up to 3 times the amount of the tax evaded; the NTS imposes an additional understatement penalty ratio of 30% and a non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax, and the unpaid tax is increased by a daily arrears surcharge of 0.022%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate form is pierced: the representative director is jointly and severally liable for the entire unpaid tax and penalties, as an 'owner-employee' responsible for the deliberate false return; the director's personal assets are subject to seizure, a travel ban (blacklisting) is issued by the Ministry of Justice Communications Office, and repatriation of the director or funds is prohibited; criminal prosecution leads to a Korean jail term; in contrast to the limited liability of the Yuhan Hoesa, the court treats the director as co-conspirator for the fraudulent scheme, and civil restitution order forces full reimbursement of the foreign-diverted funds with interest

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation, false documentation, and fraudulent intercompany payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity executes over-invoiced payments to a non-resident holding entity for simulated management-research services that are never delivered, and contemporaneous TP documentation is fabricated with false CUP references; the foreign service fee is deducted in Box 3 of the Korean corporate tax return, reducing taxable income to near zero, while the same services are recharged to Korean clients at a high margin, violating the arm's length principle under Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 12(1) and Article 6(3) of the International Tax Adjustment Act authorize the NTS to disallow the non-arm's length deduction and impose an adjustment of the taxable income; the penalty is a 30% surcharge on the adjusted amount for false TP reporting; an additional 3-year limitation extension applies; if the scheme exceeds KRW 300 million, criminal sanctions apply under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act Article 11(1) with imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to 3 times the amount dodged; foreign withholding tax at 22% on the fictitious payment is also reclaimed and imposed on the Korean payor as withholding agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The beneficial owner-directors of the Korean entity are treated as joint offenders with the non-resident recipient; courts order a piercing so that the directors' personal financial records are in scope, and any transfer to personal accounts is clawed back; the director is liable for the entire unpaid tax and penalties without any limited-company cap; travel bans are issued against the director because the NTS has classified the case as a large delinquent tax matter; criminal custodial sentence of up to 7 years is sought, and the court may additionally order compensation to the Korean tax administration for lost foreign tax credit and improperly deducted service fees

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company misuse and treaty benefit abuse in dividend and royalty restructuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign ultimate shareholders establish a Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a conduit to channel high-value dividends and digital-content royalties from Korea to a tax-heaven intermediary, where the Korean entity has no office, no full-time employees, and no substantive decision-making; the entity pays minimal corporate tax by recognizing intra-group fees, and then makes a dividend payment to the tax-haven parent claiming a 0-5% DTA rate; the NTS conducts a substance audit and determines the entity is a sham for treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4 and Article 6(2) of the International Tax Adjustment Act plus the framework of Article 172-1 of the Corporate Income Tax Act permit denial of all DTA benefits and application of the 22% domestic WHT; the NTS imposes an additional 15% penalty under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act for under-withholding of non-resident tax; the entire withholding tax uncollected is re-assessed to the Korean legal entity and its directors; criminal prosecution under Article 10(1) of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act carries imprisonment up to 5 years or fine equal to the evaded tax; the anti-abuse ruling also triggers a 40% negligence surcharge for severe omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the director approved or knew of the sham arrangement, the court pierces the Yuhan Hoesa veil: the director is personally liable for the WHT, penalties, and all interest; NTS blacklists the director's passport, imposes a travel ban, and registers the director's name on the public delinquent taxpayer list; the director's personal bank accounts and real estate are attached; if the director is a foreign national residing outside Korea, the Korean court issues a mutual legal assistance request to enforce the criminal fine and restitution order, and extradition may be pursued; the director's civil liability also includes a non-dischargeable obligation to the Korean government that survives personal bankruptcy under Korean insolvency law
